<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via loadMany (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager), loadManyKeyed (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class), MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class), loadMany (symbol, a method of class MetadataManager))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via DatabaseLoader (symbol, a top-level class), MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via MetadataManager (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b460f495215c72ccb6b6cad6607201c24cc6a4d9` — the merge of head `2126b08ccc6796b6b5c74015340cca7618b7ad33` into base `6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b460f495215c72ccb6b6cad6607201c24cc6a4d9 && git checkout b460f495215c72ccb6b6cad6607201c24cc6a4d9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661 2126b08ccc6796b6b5c74015340cca7618b7ad33 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661 && git merge --no-ff 2126b08ccc6796b6b5c74015340cca7618b7ad33

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6bbdf301f4c35739adc2333a33f3620c897b3661` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ed2915e8035a337aac4d75ede90e61302ccab952`
Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, no schema and no governed path) + packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts

Read at 2026-11-12T09:54Z: card #32521 body and its three comments (triage 6812831416, claim 6812850864, dev report 6820277215), PR #32676 body and file list, the net diff against `main` (merge base `8bfbc4ed`), and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run; every finding below is from reading the tree, and F1 says so again because its grade rests on it.

**Result: PASS with one should-fix (F1) and three nits (F2 to F4).** The fix does what the card and the epic ruling ask on a host with no declared package. F1 is one answer that moves without a FROM → TO row or a pin, on a host whose declared package is one of the two holders.

Check-runs on this head at this reading: 0 failed. Completed and green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, the three scoped lints, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI. Still running: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, · consumer gates, · debt ledger, and Lint · CI, release and engine gates. This PASS does not stand in for those; a red one among them overrides it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Bare `get` / `getDiagnosed` after the boot pass, two holders: served body → `409 ambiguous-in-environment` naming both.** Right. It is the epic ruling carried on the claim, and the same read without the pass already refused. Narrowing, first-party 0: no package, app or example calls `setDatabaseDriver`, `setDataEngine` or passes `config.driver` (grep at this head).
- **Runtime bare `/actions` door and MCP `run_action` with no merged listing: ran → `409`.** Right. The door's code is untouched; its input (`loadMany('action')`) now carries both declarations. Pinned at the door over a real manager and loader.
- **`DatabaseLoader.loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed`: one row per name → one per `(package, name)` for a contested name only.** Right, and the code matches: `unscopedTypeRows` switches key only where `namesSeveralPackagesHold` names the row's name. A legacy row keys into its own package's slot, so it is an older row of that slot and not a third holder.
- **`MetadataManager.loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed`: one per `body.name` → one per store slot for a contested name, earlier loader kept per slot.** Right. Contest is counted over every loader's items after the stamp, so two loaders each holding one package's item also hand on both.
- **Single-holder answers (red line 3): unchanged.** Holds by construction: a package-less item is never counted as a holder, an uncontested name keeps the key `name`, and `primingOrder` cannot reorder a name that hands on one item. C2 to C5 pin it, including the host-package variants.
- **`email_template` (bundled): unchanged.** Holds: `pluralEntryKey` returns `bundleEntryKey` first and `primingOrder` returns bundled types as handed.
- **Not declared: a read naming the host's own package, two holders and a package-less row.** Wrong as it stands; see F1.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata: patch` with the `!` title, the BREAKING paragraph and an ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition. This matches the rule for a non-protocol change (`Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` and keeps its banner). `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on both the PR body and the changeset, and the two texts agree. No runtime changeset is owed: the runtime diff is test-only. Check Changeset is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Deviation, two narrowing arms: accepted; both are declared with FROM → TO and pinned (rows 1 and 8).
- Deviation, content pairing added to `withLoaderEntryPackages`: accepted as the way to keep #32458's F3 rule; see F3 and F4 for its limits.
- Deviation, runtime test file: accepted; the ruling asks for the moved answer pinned where it is answered.
- Deviation, dogfood battery ran one `main` merge before this head: not judged here; the head's own check-runs are the gate and the Test Core shards are still running.
- Out-of-scope finding, package-less action row filed as one holder's customization of an object: agreed that this PR does not move it. It is not filed anywhere ("noted, not filed"); it should get a card so it is not lost.
- `security_findings: withheld` in the dev report: not visible to this review. Nothing security-relevant was found in the four files.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the spec on `main`: it makes the store's own refusal (`readStoreEntry`, D3) reachable after a boot. It takes no declared capability away.

**F1 — should-fix. On a host whose declared package is one of the two holders, a package-less row of the name replaces that holder's own item in the registry, and the answer of a read naming that package moves with no row and no pin.**
Shape: rows ALPHA, BETA and a package-less row of `helper`; `MetadataPlugin` constructed with `packageId: ALPHA`.
- `primingOrder` registers ALPHA's and BETA's items first, then the package-less one. `applyProtection` stamps that one with the host's package (it carries no `_packageId`), so `storeWriteKey` files it into ALPHA's slot and overwrites ALPHA's own item.
- TO: `get(type, 'helper', ALPHA)` answers the package-less body, in every save order. Without the pass it answers ALPHA's own body.
- FROM: ALPHA's own body, read through the loaders, whenever the package-less row was not the one saved last (two of three orders); the package-less body when it was.
- The bare read is still refused naming both, so red line 2 holds in this shape.
- Three sentences are untrue here: `primingOrder`'s jsdoc ("under a name two packages hold, the name's bare slot"; "the registry holds what a read without the pass answers, whatever order"), and PR row 7 ("a read naming a package its own item … all as without the pass"). The row-7 pins call `bootPass()` with no host package, so nothing covers it.
- This was read, not run. First step for the dev: measure it. If the answer does not move, this finding is withdrawn.
- Fix, either one: declare the row FROM → TO with its arm and pin it, if the epic seat rules that the host's stamp makes that row the host's item (the one-holder CONTROL already behaves this way); or keep a contested name's package-less item out of the host stamp so it stays in the bare slot as the jsdoc says. Reach is first-party 0. It is graded should-fix and not nit because an undeclared moved answer is the epic's own red-line clause.
- Related, no separate grade: with a host package that is neither holder, the package-less row lands in the host's slot and the bare refusal names three packages, not two.

**F2 — nit, follow-up card. In #32458's F3 shape the bare read after the pass still answers one body.** Two holders plus another row whose body says the name: nothing is stamped, the manager sees no contest, and one unstamped body is registered in the bare slot. The guess moves from BETA's body to ALPHA's (row 6b, declared, pinned at `loadMany`). The red-line-2 breach in this shape predates the PR and is not widened by it, but the card's "two holders → bare read 409" is not met there. It needs its own card; the epic seat may regrade it.

**F3 — nit, follow-up card. Content pairing is a workaround for `loadMany` carrying no row key.** `withLoaderEntryPackages` pairs a body to its keyed entry by `JSON.stringify` equality. For `DatabaseLoader` both reads come from the same rows, so it holds. A loader whose `loadMany` and `loadManyKeyed` bodies serialise differently is left unstamped with no signal and falls back to one item per name. Reading a contested name's bodies from the keyed entries directly (as the bundled path does) would remove this, and probably F2 as well (not checked).

**F4 — nit, follow-up card. `MetadataManager.loadManyKeyed` drops `packageId` from the entries it returns.** For a contested name bound by the column only it now returns two entries with the same `name` and unstamped `data`, so a caller cannot tell the holders apart and a caller keying by name collapses them (row 10's audit counts two but cannot name them). The loader's entries carry `packageId`; the manager's `{ name, data }` discards it.

Sentence-by-sentence agreement otherwise: `namesSeveralPackagesHold`, `pluralEntryKey`, the `unscopedTypeRows` jsdoc, the `admitKeyedLoaderEntries` jsdoc and the changeset bullets match the code. The no-`loadManyKeyed` fallback now loads every listed name of a slotted type; all three first-party loaders implement the keyed read, so it is reachable only from a third-party loader.

Delta review owed on F1's fix. F2 to F4 go to follow-up cards, not another round.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-skucll`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CX9R5BLZwgJDeivmA7 (contract-review sub-agent, CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER)`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `93b965e54158adf1721940941a72acc5cac032f7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, no schema and no governed path) + packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts, content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx

This is a DELTA record of comment 6820408972 (PASS at `ed2915e8`, F1 should-fix). It judges the delta `ed2915e8..93b965e5` and the unchanged tree that delta touches.

Read at 2026-11-12T11:01Z: card #32521 body and its three comments (6812831416, 6812850864, 6820277215), PR #32676 body and file list, the prior record, the four delta commits (`b9f545b5` fix, `0a3f8cbd` changeset, `53a1e2f4` merge of `main`, `93b965e5` doc paragraph) and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run. Every finding is from reading the tree, and D1's grade rests on a read, not a measurement.

**Result: PASS with one should-fix (D1).** F1 is closed for the shape it named, a package-less stored row beside two holders. The guard that closes it is wider than that shape: it also takes the host's package stamp off the host's own file item, and that moves an answer that is not declared or pinned.

Check-runs on this head at this reading: 0 failed. Completed and green: Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness. Still running: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Build Docs, the four Type Check jobs, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, two scoped lints, Live E2E UI. This PASS does not stand in for those; a red one among them overrides it.

### ① Derived judgments

- **(a) F1 closed for a package-less stored row.** Right. The pass now calls `applyProtection` with no package for an item that carries none under a name two packages hold (`contestedNames`). `storeWriteKey` then files it in the name's bare slot, because two packages already hold slots (`primingOrder` registers them first). This holds for a host declaring no package, a holder, or a third package. The bare refusal names the two holders only. Pinned: the row-7 cases now loop over four host packages, three save orders and five types, and assert the registry keys.
- **(b) Row 7a: `get(type, name, P)` where P holds no row, two holders and a package-less row saved last: the package-less body → nothing.** Right, and a narrowing, not a loosened resolution: a read that named a package holding nothing stops being answered with another holder's or the environment's body. It equals the read without the pass. It is declared FROM → TO in the PR table, carried on the `Clause-②:` line of both the changeset and the PR body, and pinned (the read naming `HOST`, on every host).
- **(c) One-holder answers: unchanged.** Holds by construction: `contestedNames` returns a name only when two or more packages hold it among the items, so a name one package holds keeps the host stamp exactly as before. The C3 expectations (measured at `efd4ea3a`) are untouched by the delta.
- **(d) Anything else in the delta.** `metadata-manager.ts` moves only through the merge of `main` (#32634); the merge is clean (empty combined diff). `database-loader.ts` and `package-slotted-store.ts` do not move. One undeclared moved answer in `plugin.ts`: see D1.
- **(e) `metadata-service.mdx`, the `loadManyKeyed` stamp paragraph.** Truthful at this head. It matches `withLoaderEntryPackages` and `pluralEntryKey`: a name two or more packages hold is handed on once per holder by `loadMany` and `loadManyKeyed`, and each body is stamped from the row whose own body it is, only where the loader's bodies of the name are exactly its rows of the name.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `@objectstack/metadata: patch` with the `!` title, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the changeset and the PR body, now naming three faces (rows 1, 7a, 8). The two texts agree. `Skills-docs: updated` names the doc page the delta edits. Check Changeset is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report; none added by the delta.
- F2 to F4 and the out-of-scope `action` row: filed as #32680 and #32681, as the prior record asked. Not re-judged.
- Dogfood battery ran before the F1 fix: not judged here; the head's Dogfood Regression Gate is green.
- `security_findings: withheld` in the dev report: not visible to this review. Nothing security-relevant was found in the delta.

### ④ Design judgment

**D1 — should-fix. The guard cannot tell a package-less stored row from the host's own file item, so under a name two packages hold the host's file item loses the host's package.**
`contestedNames` tests `storedItemPackageId(meta) === undefined`. A file-system loader's item is also unstamped; the host stamp exists to make it the host package's item ("Stamp package provenance when the host declared its package id").

Shape: host declares `packageId: P`, a file `helper.agent.yml`, and a `DatabaseLoader`. Boot 1 seeds the row `(P, helper)` from the file (the pinned "a file-system item still seeds the database loader"). Package BETA then stores its own `helper`. The file is edited. Boot 2:
- `MetadataManager.loadMany` hands on three items: the file's (no package), the row of P (the old seed) and the row of BETA. The name is contested (P, BETA).
- At this head the file item is not stamped. It is registered into the bare slot, and `register` saves it to the database loader as a new package-less row.
- TO: `get('agent', 'helper', P)` answers the old seed. `list` shows P's old body, BETA's, and the file's body as a package-less item. One more row is in `sys_metadata`.
- FROM, at `main`: `loadMany` hands on the file item alone (earlier loader), it is stamped P, fills P's slot and updates P's row. The read answers the edited file.
- FROM, at `ed2915e8`: the file item is stamped P, registered after the rows, and replaces the seed in P's slot. Same answer as `main`.
- Variant with no seeded row (rows of BETA and GAMMA only): the read naming P answers nothing, where `main` and `ed2915e8` answer the file's body.

Why it matters: the host's file edits stop reaching its own package's slot for as long as another package holds the name. This is the file-over-its-stale-seed rule that #32488 R7-C pins for `email_template`. The answer moves with no FROM → TO row and no pin (the row-7 pins use stored rows only, never a file loader), and the changeset's "no stored row changes" is untrue in this shape. Reach is first-party 0, like every other row.

This was read, not run. First step for the dev: measure boot 2 over a `rootDir` and a `DatabaseLoader`. If the read naming P answers the edited file, this finding is withdrawn.

Fix, either one: apply the guard only to an item read from a stored row (`sourceLoaderOf` names its loader) and keep the host stamp on a file item, with a pin for the shape above; or, if the epic seat rules the host's file item is the environment's own under a contested name, declare the row FROM → TO with its arm and pin it. Three sentences follow the choice: the `contestedNames` jsdoc ("it is the environment's own item"), PR row 7 ("on every host"), and the changeset bullet ("on any host").

No other finding. The doc paragraph in (e) needs no change.

Delta review owed on D1's fix.
